title: Massive Activations Line Up With the Attention Layers
hook: Hybrid linear-attention models have huge outlier activations too — and they aren't random. They spike right before every full-attention layer and plateau across the linear ones in between.
key_points: First systematic study of massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved hybrid linear-attention (HLA) LLMs.
Two architecture-aligned shapes: pre-attention spikes (PAS) just before full-attention layers, and inter-spike plateaus (ISP) persisting through linear-attention layers.
As full attention gets denser, spikes connect through plateaus and recover the stable outlier pattern of full-attention LLMs.
Reproduced across five linear-attention architectures, six hybridization configs, five data domains, and open models from 1.2B to 397B parameters.
Controlled pretraining of GDN hybrids up to 1.3B: both shapes emerge early and respond asymmetrically to output gating.
Proposed lifecycle account — PAS follows a localized write-sink-cancel process; ISP reflects delayed cancellation.
content_html: Full-attention LLMs are known to develop massive activations — a handful of hidden dimensions with enormous magnitudes that matter disproportionately for quantization and interpretability. Zunhai Su and co-authors (arXiv, August 2026) run the first systematic study of the phenomenon in hybrid linear-attention models, which interleave cheap linear-attention layers with occasional full-attention ones.
extra_html:
Two shapes

The outliers turn out to track the architecture. Pre-attention spikes (PAS) appear immediately before full-attention layers; inter-spike plateaus (ISP) are elevated values that persist through the intervening linear-attention layers. As full attention becomes denser in the hybrid, successive spikes get linked by plateaus until the pattern converges on the familiar full-attention morphology.

The authors establish this across five linear-attention architectures, six hybridization configurations, five data domains, and open hybrid models spanning 1.2B to 397B total parameters. Controlled pretraining of GDN-based hybrids up to 1.3B shows both shapes emerge early in training and respond asymmetrically to output gating: full-attention output gating strongly attenuates their magnitudes without changing the layerwise organization, while removing GDN gates amplifies them only modestly.

The mechanism they propose

A systematic-outlier analysis supports a shared lifecycle governed by when massive activations get cancelled — PAS following a localized write-sink-cancel process, ISP reflecting delayed cancellation. Code is public. For anyone quantizing or probing a hybrid model, the practical value is knowing these outliers have predictable homes rather than appearing at random.

related.title: Attention Amnesia: When Chain-of-Thought Tuning Breaks Long-Range Recall
related.hook: Fine-tuning a hybrid LLM on chain-of-thought makes it reason better but quietly forget how to find a needle in a long haystack — and the fix is to just copy back two weight matrices.

related.title: Super Weights Are Critical to Read — But Useless to Train Alone
related.hook: A handful of parameters wreck accuracy if removed. You'd think training just those would be the cheapest fine-tune ever. It isn't — it collapses the model to random guessing instead.

flashcards.prompt: Where do massive activations appear in a hybrid linear-attention LLM?

choices.text: Spiking immediately before full-attention layers, sometimes plateauing across the linear layers in between
Uniformly across all layers, independent of layer type
Only in the final layer, just before the output head

flashcards.explanation_html: The two morphologies are architecture-aligned: pre-attention spikes (PAS) before full-attention layers, and inter-spike plateaus (ISP) that persist through intervening linear-attention layers.

flashcards.prompt: What happens to these patterns as a hybrid model uses denser full attention?
flashcards.back_html: Successive spikes become increasingly connected by plateaus, eventually recovering the stable massive-activation morphology seen in full-attention LLMs.

flashcards.prompt: What lifecycle do the authors propose to explain the two shapes?
flashcards.back_html: A shared write-sink-cancel process governed by cancellation timing: spikes are localized and cancelled quickly, while plateaus reflect delayed cancellation.
